title: Unveiling Vulnerabilities of Contrastive Recommender Systems to Poisoning Attacks

problem.claim: Contrastive-learning-based recommender systems may be vulnerable to poisoning attacks that promote individual items.

gap.claim: The vulnerability of contrastive-learning-based recommender systems to item-promotion poisoning attacks is identified as insufficiently addressed.

contributions.claim: The analysis attributes the vulnerability to the uniform spread of representations caused by the InfoNCE loss.
The paper reports theoretical and empirical evidence that optimizing the InfoNCE loss favors smooth spectral values of representations.

The paper describes a dual-objective poisoning attack framework combining dispersion promotion, which encourages smoother spectral-value distributions, and rank promotion, which directly elevates target-item visibility.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report validating the threats of their attack model through extensive experimentation on four datasets.
The authors report that code is available in the ARLib repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Contrastive learning has gained prominence in recommender systems for improving recommendation accuracy and model robustness.
The paper identifies susceptibility of contrastive-learning-based recommender systems to item-promotion poisoning attacks.
The reported vulnerability is linked to representation dispersion and the InfoNCE loss's preference for smooth spectral values.
The proposed attack uses dispersion promotion and rank promotion as dual objectives.
The reported threats are evaluated on four datasets, with the broader goal of supporting more robust contrastive-learning-based recommender systems.

source_observation.claim: An optimization objective that promotes uniform or dispersed representations may create a corresponding poisoning-attack pathway.

interpretation.claim: Robustness analysis should examine whether the geometry encouraged by a training loss can be manipulated by attackers.

application.claim: Evaluate recommender-system defenses against attacks that target both representation distribution and item ranking.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these attack mechanisms generalize beyond the reported contrastive recommender-system setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, attack budgets, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the theoretical assumptions or proof details.
The abstract does not report defense performance or independently verified results.
